The working file is the complete analysis and the reports are its reader copies — each should be read in full; this message is not the analysis.

**Bottom line:** Built bottom-up from unit costs (salt, tanks, insulation, heat exchangers/pumps, controls, EPC markup), a 5 MWh molten-salt TES system comes out to roughly $178–$1,251/kWh installed (central ≈$496/kWh) — about 3.6×–30× (central ≈11×) above the published utility-scale CSP benchmark (~$42–50/kWh_t), because heat-exchanger/pump cost is governed by a near-fixed minimum engineering-package cost that doesn't shrink at small scale, while storage media/tanks (what the benchmark literature quotes) do scale down almost linearly. Levelized, TES comes out to ≈10.8¢/kWh delivered on a heat-only basis, or ≈60¢/kWh if a small-scale power block is needed to deliver electricity — against Li-ion's ≈7.1¢/kWh. Verdict (LOW confidence on magnitude, more robust on direction): at 5 MWh, lithium-ion wins decisively for any electricity-storage service; molten-salt TES only becomes viable at this scale for direct process-heat delivery or as part of a much larger aggregated system.
